summary: Real-world software requirements are often underspecified. The Clarification Challenge asks teams to build LLM-based coding assistants that recognize missing or ambiguous requirements, ask targeted clarification questions, and then produce code that better matches the user's intent.
single_track: The system may make at most one clarification turn before returning its implementation. This wording is a competition-site placeholder until the organizers confirm the exact single-turn budget and enforcement rules.
multi_track: The system may ask multiple targeted clarification questions before returning its implementation. Replace this text with the exact maximum-turn budget and any stopping rules once finalized.
private_results_message: Private test-set scores are not shown during the competition. They will be evaluated and published only at the end, after the final submission deadline.

faq.question: Which models can I use?
faq.answer: During development and validation, you may use any LiteLLM-supported hosted or locally served model. For the final private-test evaluation, the organizers will run all eligible submissions using the same fixed model and evaluation setup.

faq.question: Can I compete with my own model?
faq.answer: Yes. For the public validation leaderboard, you may evaluate your system with any LiteLLM-supported hosted or locally served model and submit the results together with your system. These results are marked as unconfirmed until they are reproduced by the organizers. Final private-test evaluation is performed by the organizers using the official fixed model and evaluation setup.

faq.question: What determines my rank?
faq.answer: TDS is the primary metric. nDCG is used only to break TDS ties. Pass@1, clarification rate, over-asking rate, and cost are reported but do not affect rank.

faq.question: Why does a leaderboard entry show no rank?
faq.answer: Organizer baselines are never ranked. Participant systems below the strongest baseline under the TDS → nDCG ordering are also shown without a rank.

faq.question: How is the private test set used?
faq.answer: The private test set is withheld during development. Organizers evaluate eligible final submissions after the competition deadline and publish private-test results at the end.

faq.question: Who may submit an ICSE solution paper?
faq.answer: Any eligible submission that receives a competition rank may submit a solution paper. The paper then follows the ICSE 2027 Competition Track review and revision process.

faq.question: Where are the technical setup instructions?
faq.answer: Installation, API keys, SDK interfaces, local model configuration, and submission examples are maintained in the competition repository.
